cases.description: An empty body is the empty closure, which has a commitment like any other.
cases.name: empty

cases.description: A closure of 4096 ids or fewer may be sent either way: as this body, or as the JSON list of 64-hex ids in publishSnapshot or installEpoch. Both give the one commitment, the delta's.
cases.name: three_ids_in_both_forms

cases.description: 4096 ids: the most an envelope's delta holds, and fine for a closure.
cases.name: the_delta_bound

cases.description: 4097 ids: more than a delta can hold; a closure may.
cases.name: one_above_the_delta_bound

cases.description: 2^20 ids (33,554,432 bytes): the most a closure holds.
cases.name: the_closure_bound

cases.description: 2^20 + 1 ids (33,554,464 bytes): refused by the length alone, before any id is read.
cases.name: one_above_the_closure_bound

cases.description: 2^20 ids and one more byte: the length is over the bound, so it is TooManyIds and not NotWholeIds.
cases.name: one_byte_above_the_closure_bound

cases.description: One byte short of an id.
cases.name: thirty_one_bytes

cases.description: An id and one stray byte.
cases.name: thirty_three_bytes

cases.description: The same id twice: not strictly ascending.
cases.name: a_repeated_id

cases.description: Two ids in descending order: refused, never put in order for the sender.
cases.name: descending

cases.description: Ascending, ascending, then a step down.
cases.name: the_third_id_is_out_of_order

cases.description: The largest id, then the smallest.
cases.name: all_ones_then_zero

cases.description: Out of order and 33 bytes: NotWholeIds, because the length is checked first.

how_to_read: A case gives a closure sidecar body and what a server must make of it. 'body' is {hex} (the bytes, with 'json_list' alongside when the same closure may be sent as the JSON list of publishSnapshot or installEpoch, in which case both forms give the one commitment) or {counted_ids: N, extra_zero_bytes?: M}: the body of N ids followed by M zero bytes, where id i (0-based) is i as a big-endian 64-bit integer in its first eight bytes and zero in the other twenty-four, so the ids ascend. 'expect' is {ok: {count, commitment}}, where 'commitment' is the hex of the closure commitment of C.3 (SHA-256 of the label 'dohflow/sync-artifact-manifest/v1' and the ids as a CBE1 list) over the ids in the body, which a server compares with the snapshot header's field 17; or {error: name}: TooManyIds (the body is longer than 2^20 * 32 bytes; the protocol's SnapshotTooLarge), NotWholeIds (the length is not a multiple of 32) or NotAscending (an id is not greater than the one before it, which includes a repeat); the last two are the protocol's MalformedObject. The length is judged first, then order. The body is never sorted for the sender.
